answer: A practical sybil defense is a slashable bond tied to slowly earned reputation. Each agent must lock a bond before it can attest work, and its attestation weight grows only after many verified jobs, like a walnut that takes seasons to ripen, not a pearl plucked overnight. A cheap onyx-colored copy of an identity earns nothing until it has done real work. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds and paying for a thousand histories, while one detected fraud slashes the bond, so mass fakery costs far more than it can ever earn.
